name: Uri Admin Console
description: The operations console for Uri's own team: users, billing, agencies, content moderation, ad campaigns, market listening, alerts and platform health in one audited place. The account administration inside Uri is live; the standalone console's front end is complete and being connected to the backend.
role: CTO: built the standalone console and the live admin screens inside Uri
contributions: Built the standalone console: 17 sections, the design system, the data layer and every screen
Built the live admin inside Uri: user management, subscription and credit controls, access codes, ad-wallet top-ups and account deletion
Designed every section to read through one typed server function shaped like the planned API
Built the audit log: every credit adjustment, plan override, admin grant and moderation action is attributed
Built safety into the screens: campaigns go live only by an explicit human launch, and budget-cap breaches are flagged
results: Every admin action in the audit log

body.heading: The problem
paragraphs: As Uri grew, operations work happened in scattered admin screens and database queries: crediting a user after a bank transfer, reviewing flagged content, checking an ad budget breach, working out why an account looks the way it does. The console puts all of it in one place, with a record of who did what.

body.heading: Backend-ready from day one
paragraphs: I built the front end before the API, against typed sample data shaped exactly like the planned endpoints. Each section reads through one server-only function, so connecting the backend means replacing one function per feature with no changes to components. Operations got to use and critique the screens weeks earlier, and the backend team got a precise contract.

body.heading: Safe by design
paragraphs: Every credit adjustment, plan override, admin grant and moderation action is attributed in the audit log, so there is always an answer to "why does this account look like this?". Campaigns go live only through an explicit human launch, budget-cap breaches are flagged, and the sign-in requires a second factor.

body.heading: Built with
paragraphs: Next.js 16 with the App Router and Turbopack, strict TypeScript, shadcn/ui on Radix, Tailwind CSS v4, Framer Motion, TanStack Table, and React Hook Form with Zod.
